messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: billing-ingest-lag alarm triggered (usage-ingest-prod). 3 customers with delayed batches > 45m. Paging on-call SRE. severity=sev2

maya (sre): oncall here, ACK. pulling dashboards + recent consumer offsets.

ci-alert-bot: Customer alert rule: automatic overage emails queued for customers c-842, c-411. suppress=false

maya (sre): quick triage: counts show retroactive spikes once delayed batches land. looks like a consumer group stall on topic 'billing-usage-prod' partitions 4-7. not seeing schema errors.

nathan (billing): joining. any evidence of token count double-ingestion or just delayed delivery?

maya (sre): initial check — counts in raw stream are low for window 2026-03-16T02:00..03:00, then a bulk emit at 2026-03-16T03:12. SQL sample:

```
SELECT window_start, sum(token_count) as tokens
FROM billing_raw.events
WHERE window_start >= '2026-03-16'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
-- returns: 02:00 -> 120k, 03:00 -> 1.5M (spike)
```

nathan (billing): that matches delayed batching, not duplication for that query. can you post consumer lag?

maya (sre): consumer offsets snapshot:

```
topic: billing-usage-prod partition:4 lag: 1,124,000
partition:5 lag: 980,400
partition:6 lag: 1,200,789
partition:7 lag: 1,050,012
consumer_group: billing-ingest-consumer
```

maya (sre): hypothesis: backlog + transient GC on one consumer pod + autoscaler not triggering fast enough. immediate mitigation options: 1) increase consumer parallelism (scale consumer pods) 2) pause overage-alerts while backfill runs 3) throttled replays.

selena (support): which customers are showing overage flags now? do we need to send hold messages?

maya (sre): affected customers (observed flags): c-842 (enterprise), c-411 (startup), c-1298 (mid-market). c-842 already queued for overage email. recommend suppressing outbound alerts for 30m while we reconcile.

nathan (billing): I'll flip suppression for outbound alerts now and scale consumers. running:

```
# scale consumers
kubectl scale deploy billing-ingest-consumer --replicas=6 -n prod
# flip alert suppression
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/alerts/suppress -d '{"rule":"overage-outbound","ttl":1800}'
```

nathan (billing): scaled to 6, suppression API returned 200. observing offset consumption starting.

maya (sre): evidence of progress: offsets decreasing, recent logs: `processed 250k msgs in 30s`, CPU on consumers spiked to 85% and now settling.

ci-alert-bot: suppression applied: rule=overage-outbound ttl=1800s by nathan.

selena (support): thanks — I'll hold outbound comms and notify account teams for c-842 and c-411 that we're investigating and suppressing emails for 30m.

nathan (billing): launching targeted backfill job for 2026-03-16 02:00 window to smooth counts, running in low-rate mode to avoid bursty downstream load. Command: `jobs/backfill --topic billing-usage-prod --from 2026-03-16T02:00 --to 2026-03-16T03:30 --rate 1000/s`

maya (sre): monitoring metrics: raw ingest lag metric dropped from ~1.15M to ~80k in ~4m after scaling. backfill steady at 800 msg/s.

nathan (billing): logs from backfill: `backfill: window 02:15 -> enqueued 48k events, dedup-check passed` — no duplicates detected so far.

maya (sre): action items for now: - keep consumers scaled until lag < 5k - continue backfill until window reconciled - alert suppression remains active for 30m - postmortem if cause is autoscaler misfire

selena (support): can we automate a customer-facing note if suppression lifts and overage emails were prevented? need template. I'll draft.

maya (sre): update at +20m: lag now 2.1k across partitions, backfill complete for 02:00..03:30 windows. counts reconciled, no duplicate inflations seen in sample verification.

nathan (billing): removing suppression now. API call returned 200. will re-run reconciliation job to ensure billing totals match and flag adjustments applied.

ci-alert-bot: suppression removed by nathan. queued outbound overage emails canceled during suppression window were not sent.

selena (support): notifying customers: sent note to c-842 and c-411 that they may see adjusted usage and that we prevented erroneous overage emails. account teams looped in.

maya (sre): resolution summary: incident closed (mitigated) — root cause likely transient consumer pod GC + slow autoscaler. severity downgraded to sev3. follow-ups: postmortem to include (1) autoscaler tuning, (2) add a backpressure metric alert earlier, (3) ensure suppression playbook steps are in runbook.

nathan (billing): reopening a billing ticket to run full reconciliation and to validate invoice pipeline. ticket: BILL-4523.

maya (sre): thanks all. I'll create the incident report and assign follow-ups. tagging @postmortem-team. :white_check_mark:
